manifest.name: dsh-asa-agent
manifest.description: Bridge the Asa self-learning research agent into DeepSeek Harness. Mounts the host's MCP client against Asa's Streamable HTTP endpoint (default http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp), surfacing asa_research, asa_message and asa_status as mcp__asa__* tools, and adds an asa_doctor diagnostic plus a system-prompt primer.
manifest.author: Memkist

bundle.text:
# dsh-asa-agent bundle patch: inserts the Asa (self-learning research agent)
# plugin into a profile's layer stack. It mounts the harness's
# @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client against Asa's Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint, so
# asa_research / asa_message / asa_status surface as mcp__asa__* tools; it also
# registers the native asa_doctor diagnostic and a system-prompt primer.
#
# Override this row in a higher-priority profile layer (id-targeted patch) to
# set url / serverName / token / mcp / primer / toolCallTimeoutMs /
# failOnStartupError / doctorTimeoutMs. `config` is replaced wholesale, not
# deep-merged, so restate every key you want to keep.
- insert:
    - id: dsh-asa-agent
      name: 'dsh-asa-agent'

readme.text:
**Asa's research pipeline, a full Asa agent turn, and Asa's health stats inside a DSH session — three MCP tools and a doctor, bridged from one local endpoint.**

`dsh-asa-agent` is a DeepSeek Harness plugin bundle. It mounts the host's `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` (transport: `streamable-http`) against the MCP server Asa's gateway already serves at `POST /mcp`, and adds one native tool that tells you whether that bridge is healthy.

> **Status — v0.1.0, not yet installed.** This documentation set was written against Asa 0.1.0 and the DSH desktop profile as of 2026-10-24. The plugin has not been installed into a live profile yet, so the quickstart below is the install *procedure*, not a report of a completed run. Every step that needs your approval says so explicitly.

| Tool | Type | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `mcp__asa__asa_research` | bridged MCP tool | Runs Asa's recursive research pipeline on a topic: plan → web search → fetch → ingest into the Vectorless RAG knowledge base → analyze with confidence → synthesize a cited report. Returns the report path and run stats. Can take minutes. |
| `mcp__asa__asa_message` | bridged MCP tool | Sends a message to Asa and returns its reply. Pass `session_id` to continue a conversation. Accepts up to 10 attachments. |
| `mcp__asa__asa_status` | bridged MCP tool | Asa health and memory statistics, including whether Docker is reachable. |
| `asa_doctor` | native DSH tool | Probes the configured gateway and reports reachability, the tools it discovered, and hints for fixing a failure. |

**In plain terms:** DSH gains three tools that *are* Asa, and one tool that tells you why the other three aren't answering.

The first three names come from DSH's MCP naming rule, `mcp__<serverName>__<rawName>`. Asa's server is named `asa` and its tools are already named `asa_research`, `asa_message`, `asa_status` — so the names read `asa` twice. That is correct, not a typo. Change `serverName` in the plugin config and the prefix follows it.
**In plain terms:** the tool name is "the MCP namespace" + "the tool's own name", and both happen to be called `asa`.

readme.section: Why three tools and not fifteen
readme.text: An earlier planning document for this integration proposed a *new* stdio MCP server with roughly fifteen tools (`asa.recall`, `asa.record`, `asa.audit`, `asa.sleep`, `asa.forget`, `asa.kb.*`, `asa.skills.*`, `company.*`, `asa.ask`, `asa.message.send`). **That server does not exist.** None of those tools are on Asa's MCP endpoint today.

readme.section: Why three tools and not fifteen
readme.text:
What exists is Asa's gateway MCP server — Streamable HTTP, stateless JSON mode, exactly three tools — and this plugin bridges it without adding a second server in the middle. The invented surface is tracked as [roadmap](#roadmap--not-implemented) below and is labelled not implemented.

**In plain terms:** the docs describe the three tools that work, and file the fifteen that don't under "not built yet" instead of pretending.

**Path conventions:** `<asa-repo>` is the path to your Asa checkout and `<plugin-dir>` is the path to this repository as checked out on your machine. They are placeholders, not real directories — substitute your own absolute paths.

You need: a local Asa checkout, a DSH desktop profile, and a free terminal. Asa's own README lists **Node 22+** and **Python 3.12+** as its prerequisites.

In a terminal you can leave running:

```powershell
cd <asa-repo>
npm run setup
npm run dev:gateway
```

`npm run setup` is first-run only and is idempotent — skip it on later runs. `npm run dev:gateway` blocks, serving the gateway on `http://localhost:8787`; leave it running and use a second terminal for the next command.

**In plain terms:** Asa is the server here. Nothing works until it is running.

In a second terminal:

```powershell
Invoke-RestMethod http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/health
```

You should see `ok : True`, `name : asa` and `version : 0.1.0`. `/api/health` is an unauthenticated route on loopback — a useful smoke check before you involve DSH at all.

**In plain terms:** this asks Asa "are you alive?" in a way that needs no token and no MCP client.

readme.section: 3. Install the plugin bundle — this needs your approval
readme.text:
Plugin installation goes through the harness, not a shell `npm install` into the profile. In DSH, install the bundle with the `plugin_manager` tool's `install_bundle` action, passing the plugin directory as the target:

```json
{
  "action": "install_bundle",
  "target": "<plugin-dir>"
}

This block is **not a shell command** — it is the argument object for a `plugin_manager` tool call, shown so you can see the exact target path.

readme.section: 3. Install the plugin bundle — this needs your approval
readme.text:
macOS and Windows surface a **plugin-installation approval prompt**; you have to accept it. If the result names a `pendingBuilds` entry, that install script needs its own explicit approval before it runs. Neither step is unattended.

**In plain terms:** DSH asks you "may I install this?" and you have to say yes. Nothing installs silently.

In a DSH session, call `mcp__asa__asa_status` — no arguments — and then run `asa_doctor`, which also takes none. The argument object is the same for both:

```json
{}
```

The first call proves the bridge carries traffic; the second proves it is pointed at the right place and tells you what to fix if it isn't.

**In plain terms:** one call asks Asa for its stats, the other asks the plugin whether the wiring is sound.

`asa_status` returns JSON text shaped like this:

```json
{
  "docker": true,
  "kb": { "documents": 42 },
  "mind": { "...": "memory statistics" }

The keys come from Asa: `docker` is a boolean from its Docker probe, and `kb` / `mind` are its knowledge-base and cognitive-memory statistics. `asa_doctor` reports reachability, the tools it discovered, and fix hints instead.
**In plain terms:** a healthy answer shows Docker's state plus Asa's memory counters; a broken one points you at the next step.

| Key | Default | Why you'd change it |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `ASA_MCP_URL` env, else loopback using `ASA_GATEWAY_PORT` (default `8787`) | Asa runs on another port or another machine. |
| `serverName` | `asa` | You already bridge another server named `asa`. |
| `token` | *(unset)* | Asa is remote, so the pairing token is required. |
| `mcp` | `true` | Keep `asa_doctor` but skip the MCP bridge. |
| `primer` | `true` | You don't want a system-prompt section about Asa. |
| `toolCallTimeoutMs` | `600000` | Research takes longer than 10 minutes on your machine. |
| `failOnStartupError` | `false` | You want harness startup to fail loudly when Asa is down. |
| `doctorTimeoutMs` | `15000` | The probe times out on a slow machine. |

Override any of these in your profile's patch layer under `id: dsh-asa-agent`. Note that a patch row's `config` is **replaced wholesale, not deep-merged**, so restate every key you want to keep.

**In plain terms:** you can point this at a different Asa, give it a token, or turn a piece off — and every default is chosen so that doing nothing still works on a stock local Asa.

If the gateway is on loopback, **Asa's own auth lets the call through without a token** — that is Asa's design, not a plugin weakness, and it is why the default URL is `127.0.0.1`. Point the plugin at a remote Asa and you must supply the pairing token. `asa_message` does not call a read-only API: it runs a **full Asa agent turn**, so its blast radius is Asa's own tool surface (workspace reads and writes, sandbox execution, web fetches). Before exposing anything beyond localhost, know that the plugin adds no transport security of its own: over plain `http://` your pairing token and every tool payload are readable on the network.
**In plain terms:** on the same machine, Asa trusts you without a password. The message tool is a whole agent, not a lookup.

- **No `mcp__asa__*` tools in the session** — the bundle isn't installed or enabled, or the bridge failed at startup. Run `asa_doctor`; if that tool is missing too, the plugin itself isn't loaded.
- **`asa_doctor` says unreachable** — Asa's gateway isn't running, or `url` points somewhere else. Start it with `npm run dev:gateway`.
- **401 "pairing required"** — `url` points at a non-loopback host (a LAN IP, for example) without a token. Use `127.0.0.1` or set `token`.

- **A call seems to hang for minutes** — `asa_research` legitimately takes minutes; `toolCallTimeoutMs` defaults to ten. If a call parks close to ten minutes and comes back without doing anything, Asa stopped on its own `ask_user` consent prompt and there was nobody in the Asa window to answer it: the turn resumes as "not confirmed". Answer the prompt in Asa's UI, or set Asa's `ASA_ASK_TIMEOUT_MS` lower so unanswerable prompts fail fast.
**In plain terms:** almost every failure is either "Asa isn't running" or "the URL is wrong" — check those two first.

This README is the complete public guide: install, configuration, security and the failures people actually hit. A longer reference set — architecture walkthrough, exhaustive tool reference, deployment and consent-hazard notes — is maintained privately and is not part of this repository.
Nothing in this table exists as an Asa MCP tool today. It is the surface the earlier planning document proposed; treat it as a wish list, not an API.

| Proposed | Layer | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `asa.recall`, `asa.record`, `asa.audit`, `asa.sleep`, `asa.forget` | cognitive memory loop | **not implemented** |
| `asa.kb.query`, `asa.kb.ingest`, `asa.kb.list` | knowledge base | **not implemented** |
| `asa.skills.list`, `asa.skills.read` | skills | **not implemented** |
| `company.recall`, `company.remember` | company brain | **not implemented** |
| `asa.ask`, `asa.message.send` | bounded Q&A loop, fire-and-forget inbox | **not implemented** |
| `asa.spawn`, `asa.run` | full autonomous loop | **not implemented** |
| stdio transport (spawned per session) | transport | **not implemented** — v0.1.0 is Streamable HTTP only |

For context: Asa's MCP surface *shrank* before this plugin existed. Its repo's own check (`npm run check:mcp`) asserts that `asa_recall`, `asa_ingest` and `asa_sandbox_run` are **absent** from the tool list. A roadmap entry that reintroduces them is a design proposal, not a restoration.

**In plain terms:** the memory and knowledge-base tools people expected are not there — Asa removed some of them on purpose, and the rest were never built.
